'''Lorraine S. Symington''' {{Post-nominals|country=GBR|FRS}} is a British-American [[geneticist]]. As the Harold S. Ginsberg Professor and Director of Graduate Studies of Microbiology & Immunology at [[Columbia University]], her laboratory uses genetic, biochemical and molecular approaches to understand mechanisms of homology-directed double-strand break repair using the yeast Saccharomyces cerevisiae as an experimental system.

==Early life and education==
Symington completed her [[Bachelor of Science]] degree from the [[University of Sussex]] and her PhD in genetics from the [[University of Glasgow]]. Following her graduating, she moved to North America and completed her postdoctoral training in DNA biochemistry with [[Richard Kolodner]] at [[Harvard Medical School]] and in yeast genetics with [[Tom Petes]] at the [[University of Chicago]].<ref name="lectures">{{cite web |title=Mechanisms of Homologous Recombination |url=https://mendellectures.muni.cz/home/lectures/20142015#_lect_back1 |website=mendellectures.muni.cz |access-date=March 15, 2021}}</ref>

==Career==
Symington joined the faculty at [[Columbia University]] in 1988.<ref name="lectures"/> Throughout her tenure at Columbia, her laboratory uses genetic, biochemical and molecular approaches to understand mechanisms of homology-directed double-strand break repair using the yeast Saccharomyces cerevisiae as an experimental system.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Lee |first1=Andrew H. |last2=Symington |first2=Lorraine S. |last3=Fidock |first3=David A. |author-link3=David A. Fidock |date=September 7, 2014 |title=DNA Repair Mechanisms and Their Biological Roles in the Malaria Parasite Plasmodium falciparum |journal=[[Microbiology and Molecular Biology Reviews]] |volume=78 |issue=3 |pages=469–486 |doi=10.1128/MMBR.00059-13 |pmc=4187680 |pmid=25184562 |doi-access=free}}</ref> In 2018, Symington was elected to the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]] for her "major, lasting contributions toward our understanding of mechanisms of DNA-damage induced break repair."<ref>{{cite web |title=Lorraine Symington Elected to American Academy of Arts and Sciences |url=https://www.cuimc.columbia.edu/news/lorraine-symington-elected-american-academy-arts-and-sciences |website=cuimc.columbia.edu |access-date=March 15, 2021 |date=April 23, 2018}}</ref> During the [[COVID-19 pandemic]], Symington was elected to the [[National Academy of Sciences]] for her genetics research.<ref name="NAS">{{cite web |title=Five Columbia Faculty Join the Ranks of the National Academy of Sciences |url=https://news.columbia.edu/news/five-columbia-faculty-join-ranks-national-academy-sciences |website=news.columbia.edu |access-date=March 15, 2021 |date=March 2, 2020}}</ref> She was elected a [[Fellow of the Royal Society]] in 2024.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Professor Lorraine Symington FRS |url=https://royalsociety.org/people/lorraine-symington-36801/ |access-date=2024-05-20 |website=Royal Society |language=en}}</ref>
